title: Vasquez: private faith of the promise necessary alongside Catholic faith for hope and justification
source_text: XL. Est autem hic observandum Gabrielem Vasquez non solum agnoscere fiduciam esse fidei vivae partem, sed etiam illum nomen fidei tribuere persuasioni illi, qua aliquis per veram poenitentiam se ad Deum convertens, confidit Deum sibi peccata remissurum, seque justificandum esse. Nam ad justificationem docet non tantum conducere, sed necessariam esse, non solum fidem Catholicam dogmatum, historiae, & promissionum quae universe factae sunt, sed etiam fidem privatam promissionis, qua quisque credat sibi Deum non defuturum, neque negaturum auxilium efficax, & se tandem a Deo justificandum. Nam, inquit, si aliquis existimaret Deum negaturum auxilium efficax ad salutem, omnis ad justificationem progressus & dispositio impediretur, ut manifeste constat. Inter reliqua enim necessaria ad justificationem primam debet esse spes veniae; haec autem sine fide peculiari esse non potest. Nam quamvis aliquis crederet ea quae universe promissa sunt, nempe, vere poenitentibus peccata remitti, & poenitentiae adeoque operibus bonis a Deo obtineri veniam & justificationem; tamen nisi etiam credat se iis operibus quae exercet a Deo veniam consecuturum, quae sane est fides peculiaris promissionis, non poterit nunc veniam sibi a Deo sperare, ac proinde neque justificationis compos erit; siquidem spes non minus necessaria est dispositio ad justificationem quam fides. Quocirca fidem illam quam Concilium Tridentinum Sessione sexta, cap. 8. docet esse humanae salutis initium & fundamentum, & radicem omnis justificationis, & sine qua cum Apostolo dicit esse impossibile placere Deo, & ad consortium filiorum pervenire, fidem, inquam, illam non solum esse fidem Catholicam & dogmaticam, sed etiam fidem privatam promissionis; & pertendit verba Concilii de utraque exponenda & intelligenda esse, ut videre est cap. 5. Disputationis 210. jam citatae.
pass_a_gloss: Here it should be observed that Gabriel Vasquez not only acknowledges that trust is a part of living faith, but also gives the name of faith to that persuasion by which someone converting to God through true repentance trusts that God will remit his sins to him and that he is to be justified. For he teaches that for justification there is needed not only Catholic faith of dogmas, history, and promises made universally, but also a private faith of the promise by which each person believes God will not fail him, will not deny efficacious help, and that he will at last be justified by God. For, he says, if someone thought God would deny efficacious help for salvation, every progress and disposition to justification would be hindered, as is plainly clear. Among the other things necessary for first justification there must be hope of pardon; but this cannot exist without a peculiar faith. For although someone believed the things promised universally — namely that sins are remitted to the truly penitent, and that by repentance and so by good works pardon and justification are obtained from God — yet unless he also believes that by the works he exercises he will obtain pardon from God, which is indeed a peculiar faith of the promise, he will not now be able to hope for pardon from God for himself, and therefore will not be a partaker of justification either; since hope is no less a necessary disposition to justification than faith. Therefore that faith which the Council of Trent Session six, chapter 8, teaches is the beginning and foundation of human salvation and the root of all justification, and without which with the Apostle it says it is impossible to please God and to come to the fellowship of sons — that faith, he maintains, is not only Catholic and dogmatic faith but also private faith of the promise; and he holds that the Council words are to be explained and understood of both, as may be seen in chapter 5 of Disputation 210 already cited.
pass_b_english: Vasquez not only puts fiducia inside living faith but names as faith the penitent persuasion that God will remit one sins and justify him.

Beside Catholic faith of universal dogmas and promises he requires a private promise-faith that God will not fail with efficacious help; without that peculiar faith, hope of pardon — itself a necessary disposition — cannot stand, so Trent sess. 6 c. 8 faith as salvation beginning/root covers both Catholic and private promise-faith (Disp. 210.5).
